creator: Alexander Terp
description:
**In flight in worktree `rad4`.** Two cards on the main board, and they're one thread:

- `RAD-393: cmds: support sub commands` (in `next`) - `command add file:` is not currently possible
- `RAD-394: cmds: support nested command definitions` (in `in-progress`) - the nesting form:

```rad
command add:
  verbose bool
  command file:  // << this
    on_call on_add_file
```

**Sequence this against the default-command card in this column.** They touch the same routing and help-generation code, and the review flags that multi-level dispatch ripples into default-command semantics. Landing one and then rebasing the other is cheaper than interleaving; decide which leads before starting.

Two things worth confirming early, both cheap and both affecting the design:

- A command block currently **requires a `calls` line to parse at all.** Nested parents may have no handler of their own, so decide whether `calls` becomes optional for a parent that only routes.
- Per-command and shared variadics alongside commands now pass `rad check`, so a comment at `peer:368-369` claiming they're blocked may be stale. This is check #2 on the verify-first runtime-checks card - get that answer first, since it determines whether variadic support inside nested commands is new work or already there.

Help generation is the part most likely to be underestimated: `--help` at each level needs to list that level's subcommands and its own args, and the existing generator assumes one level.

---

### Current state

Verified 2026-08-10 against worktree `/Users/amterp/src/rad4` (branch `rad4`).

**Nothing is committed.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD main` succeeds and `git rev-list --count HEAD..main` is 81, so branch `rad4` carries zero unique commits and sits 81 commits behind `main`. The whole feature lives as *staged but uncommitted* changes in that working tree. Commit them before doing anything else - one `git checkout` there loses the lot.

Staged: 13 files, +384/-109 - `SYNTAX.md`, `core/args.go`, `core/command_types.go`, `core/interpreter.go`, `core/runner.go`, `docs-web/docs/guide/script-commands.md`, `go.mod`, `rts/check/binder.go`, `rts/check/type_check.go`, `rts/converter.go`, `rts/rl/ast_children.go`, `rts/rl/ast_dump.go`, `rts/rl/ast_types.go`. Plus two **untracked** snapshot files that are part of the work: `core/testing/snapshots/args/nested_cmds.snap` (7 cases) and `rts/check/snapshots/commands.snap` (2 cases).

It builds and it is green. `go build ./...` is clean; `go test ./core/testing/... ./rts/... ./radls/lstesting/...` passes all six packages.

**It depends on an uncommitted grammar change.** `go.mod` carries `replace github.com/amterp/tree-sitter-rad => /Users/amterp/src/tree-sitter-rad`. That checkout is on branch `main` with uncommitted edits to `grammar.js`, `src/grammar.json`, `src/parser.c`, `src/node-types.json`, `FIELDS.md`, `NODES.md`. The grammar change turns the `cmd_block` body into a choice:

```js
choice(
  field("calls", $.cmd_calls),          // leaf command
  repeat1(field("command", $.cmd_block)), // namespace command
)
```

Commit and release that in tree-sitter-rad, then point rad's `go.mod` at the released version. AGENTS.md forbids committing the `replace` directive, and `./dev --release` refuses to release with one present.

What the staged work implements - the **nested** form only (RAD-394). A command is a leaf (has `calls`) or a namespace (contains nested `command` blocks, no `calls`); a namespace's own args are shared and inherited by every descendant. `rl.CmdBlock.Callback` became `*CmdCallback` (nil means namespace), `SubCmds []*CmdBlock` was added alongside an `IsNamespace()` and a `WalkCmds` pre-order helper. `ScriptCommand` gained `SubCmds`, `Parent`, `HasCallback`. `core/runner.go` grew `registerCommandTree` (mirrors the command tree onto Ra recursively) and `resolveInvokedCommand` (descends used-children to the terminal command, then collects inherited args root-to-leaf, leaf wins on name collision). A new `AsSharedNamespaceArg` mode (`core/args.go:49`) registers namespace args as Ra globals so Ra cascades them into every child.

Where it stopped - three known gaps:

1. **Shared-arg help rendering is a deliberate TODO, and it is upstream work in `ra`.** The comment on `registerCommandTree` records it: Ra renders globals under "Global options" and hides them in short help, so a namespace's shared args do not appear under "Command args" where they belong. Per AGENTS.md this gets fixed in `~/src/ra`, not worked around here.
2. **The flattened form is not implemented.** `command remote add:` on one line - that is RAD-393, still in `next` on the main board. Only the indented/nested form parses.
3. **`rad fmt` is untested against nested blocks.** `rad fmt` did not exist at rad4's base commit (`./bin/radd fmt` there prints `Unknown file or command: fmt`); it does on `main`. `rts/radfmt` is untouched by the staged diff, and `rts/radfmt/printer.go:15-25` lists `cmd_block` among the constructs deliberately left unformatted - they fall through to verbatim, which is structurally safe. So this is probably a non-issue, but confirm after rebasing that `rad fmt` does not corrupt a nested block.

The 81-commit rebase is the first real chunk of work, and it is not cosmetic - `rad fmt`, the args-block formatter and the built-in-command guide all landed on `main` after rad4's base.

### Orientation

The pipeline for a command block, in order:

1. **Grammar** - `tree-sitter-rad`'s `grammar.js`, rule `cmd_block`. Produces a CST.
2. **AST** - `rts/converter.go`, `convertCmdBlock` / `convertCmdCallback`, building `rl.CmdBlock` from `rts/rl/ast_types.go`. Adding a field means also touching `rts/rl/ast_children.go` and `rts/rl/ast_dump.go` (the latter feeds `--ast-tree`).
3. **Static check** - `rts/check/binder.go` (`bindFile` declares every command arg as a `SymCmdArg` so callbacks can reference them; `visitCmdBlock` resolves the callback) and `rts/check/type_check.go`.
4. **Runtime registration** - `core/command_types.go` `FromCmdBlock` converts `rl.CmdBlock` into `ScriptCommand`; `core/runner.go` `registerCommands` walks `r.scriptData.Commands` and registers each onto the `ra` root command `RRootCmd` via `ra.NewCmd(...)` + `parent.RegisterCmd(raCmd)`. `RegisterCmd` returns a `*bool` "was used" pointer, stored in `r.cmdInvocations`. Args are registered with a mode from `core/args.go` - `AsScriptFlagOnly` for script-level `args:` (valid at every level, flag syntax only), `AsCommandArg` for a leaf's own args (positional + flag), `AsSharedNamespaceArg` for namespace args (Ra globals, so they cascade).
5. **Dispatch** - `core/runner.go` `parseAndExecute` calls `RRootCmd.ParseOrExit`, then finds the invoked command and hands its args to `interpreter.InitArgs` before running the callback.

Note the constraint from AGENTS.md: **`rts` must not import `core`.** The AST and checker cannot know anything about `ra` or `ScriptCommand`.

### Where to start

- Read the staged diff first: `cd /Users/amterp/src/rad4 && git diff --cached`. It is the design, written out.
- `/Users/amterp/src/rad4/core/runner.go` - `registerCommands`, `registerCommandTree`, `resolveInvokedCommand`, and the namespace guard in `parseAndExecute`.
- `/Users/amterp/src/rad4/core/command_types.go` - `ScriptCommand`, `FromCmdBlock`.
- `/Users/amterp/src/rad4/rts/rl/ast_types.go` - `CmdBlock`, `CmdCallback`, `WalkCmds`.
- `/Users/amterp/src/rad4/rts/converter.go` - `convertCmdBlock` (around line 925).
- `/Users/amterp/src/rad4/core/args.go:43-49` - the arg-mode enum, including `AsSharedNamespaceArg`.
- `/Users/amterp/src/tree-sitter-rad/grammar.js` - the `cmd_block` rule.
- Design doc: `docs/thinking/commands.md`. The nested-vs-flattened comparison is at lines 425-497 and matches what rad4 built (Style 1). The doc's suggestion to "possibly support both" is what RAD-393 would deliver.

### How to verify

Build is `make build`, producing `bin/radd`. A bare `rad` is the installed release and will not have your changes.

```sh
cd /Users/amterp/src/rad4
make build
go test ./core/testing/... ./rts/... ./radls/lstesting/...
```

Snapshot suites that own this feature:

- `core/testing/snapshots/args/nested_cmds.snap` - end-to-end runs. Regenerate with
  `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=args/nested_cmds`
- `rts/check/snapshots/commands.snap` - checker diagnostics. Regenerate with
  `go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots -update=commands`

The `=` is required - a bare `-update -run X` swallows `-run` as the update value. Under `-update=...` mismatches in non-targeted files still fail, so unrelated regressions cannot be baked in silently. Always review the `.snap` diff.

Manual smoke test - write a scratch script and run it:

```sh
./bin/radd /tmp/nested.rad remote add origin https://x --timeout 5
./bin/radd /tmp/nested.rad remote -h      # should list sub-commands
./bin/radd /tmp/nested.rad remote          # should error, listing sub-commands
```

Useful flags: `--cst-tree` (grammar output), `--ast-tree` (post-conversion), `--src`.

### Done when

- The tree-sitter-rad grammar change is committed and released, and rad's `go.mod` references the released version with **no `replace` directive**.
- The rad-side work is committed on a branch rebased onto current `main`.
- `make all` passes, and `make verify-generated` is clean (CI runs it).
- Both snapshot suites above cover: leaf dispatch under a namespace, inherited flag before and after the sub-command, inherited default, three-level nesting, bare-namespace error, namespace `-h`, top-level `-h`. Those seven cases already exist in `nested_cmds.snap` - keep them green rather than rewriting them.
- Shared args render under "Command args" in help, not "Global options" - which means the `ra` fix has landed and been released, not patched around in rad.
- `SYNTAX.md` documents the nested form (already drafted in the staged diff) and `docs-web/docs/guide/script-commands.md` matches.
- `rad fmt` round-trips a nested command block without corrupting it.
- Decide explicitly whether RAD-393's flattened form ships in the same change or as a follow-up, and say so on that card.
- Per AGENTS.md, invoke the Rad Docs Maintainer subagent - this is a user-facing syntax change.

### Watch out for

- **The uncommitted-work trap.** Both the rad changes and the grammar changes are uncommitted, in two different repos. Commit both before rebasing, experimenting, or running anything destructive.
- **`replace` directives are never committed.** Iterate locally with it, strip it before committing.
- **Two failure mechanisms, pick the right one.** `RadPanic` for catchable, data-driven user errors; `emitError*` for hard exits on programming errors. A bare-namespace invocation is a usage error and currently routes through `RP.UsageErrorExit`.
- **Registration order matters.** `RegisterCmd` copies the parent's globals into the child, so a namespace's shared args must be registered on the parent *before* its children are registered. `registerCommandTree` already does this; preserve the ordering if you refactor.
- **Ra marks every command on the invoked path as used**, not just the leaf - that is why `resolveInvokedCommand` descends rather than taking the first match. A naive "first used command wins" loop silently dispatches the namespace.
- **`rl.WalkCmds` exists so nested commands are never silently skipped.** Any new code that iterates `file.Cmds` should use it. A plain `for _, cmd := range file.Cmds` is the bug shape here - it compiles, passes shallow tests, and quietly ignores everything nested.
- **The card's premise about `calls` being mandatory is confirmed and already resolved** - the grammar previously required `field("calls", $.cmd_calls)` unconditionally; the staged change makes it a choice. Nothing left to decide there.
- **Verify variadic support separately.** The card points at check #2 on the verify-first runtime-checks card. rad4's base is 81 commits old, so run that check against `main`, not against rad4.
title: Support nested and sub commands
